newsitem.title: USA: Ashland's Nigeria woes still not resolved.
newsitem.headline: Ashland's Nigeria woes still not resolved.

text.p: Ashland Inc's efforts to sell its last upstream business, located in Nigeria, remain tangled, but the company's top executive said Monday that he remains sanguine the "misunderstanding" will be cleared up.

"We think there's a misunderstanding. We think there's a communication problem. But we think we'll clear up the misunderstanding," Ashland Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Chellgren told Reuters.
He said his company continues to seek a meeting with Nigerian officials, but he declined to discuss the company's ongoing efforts and frustrations in doing so thus far.

Ashland was negotiating to sell its nearly 20,000 barrels per day of equity crude production to France's privately-held Pernenco Investments SA until last month, when Nigeria's oil minister ordered the cancellation of Ashland production contracts and work permits in that West African state.
Analysts reckon Ashland could net anywhere between $50 and $60 million in a sale of the assets, assuming of course the company successfully straightens out its difficulties.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
